verses.1: For the chief musician, on the lyre. A psalm by David.
verses.2: I will praise the LORD from the depths of my heart; I will proclaim all your wondrous deeds.
verses.3: I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing your name, Most High.
verses.4: When my enemies turned their backs, they stumbled and were destroyed in your presence.
verses.5: For you have established my justice and my judgment; you have sat enthroned as the judge of righteousness.
verses.6: You rebuked the nations, you destroyed the wicked, you erased their name forever and ever.
verses.7: Their weapons of war are broken, their cities are torn down; their memory perishes with a cry.
verses.8: But the LORD reigns forever; he has established his throne for justice.
verses.9: He will judge the world in righteousness, he will rule the nations with fairness.
verses.10: And the LORD will be a refuge for the oppressed, a helper in times of trouble.
verses.11: Those who know your name will trust in you, for you do not abandon those who seek you, O LORD.
verses.12: Sing to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim among the nations his deeds.
verses.13: For he remembers the cries of the afflicted; he does not forget their pleas.
verses.14: Be merciful to me, O LORD; see my distress from my enemies. Uplift me from the gates of death.
verses.15: That I may declare all your praises in the gates of the daughter of Zion, and rejoice in your salvation.
verses.16: The nations have been snared in their own schemes; they have been caught in the trap they made.
verses.17: The LORD knows the judgment of the wicked; in the works of their own hands, the evildoer is ensnared. Selah.
verses.18: Let the wicked return to Sheol, all the nations that have forgotten God.
verses.19: For the poor will not be forgotten forever, the hope of the afflicted will not perish for good.
verses.20: Arise, O LORD; let not the human grow strong. Let the nations be judged in your presence.
verses.21: You have set instruction for them, O LORD; let the nations know that they are human. Selah.

notes:
Notes
- v. 17: "Selah" is a musical or liturgical term of uncertain meaning, retained here as in the Hebrew.
